acceptance: A real fork PR adding a valid bundle under results-data/bundles/ and updating results-data/corpus-inventory.json against develop triggers validate-submission.yml and receives its summary comment.
Heavy Python unit/medium/correctness code lanes are skipped on that fork PR while all required develop ruleset checks reach a green/mergeable state (aside from the intentional manual-review hold).
Auto-merge is mechanically blocked (no-auto-merge label applied and enforced by hold) until a maintainer manually reviews and lifts the hold.

Either (a) an owner-approved real bundle merges and is verified in the subsequent site-inputs bundle + benchbox-site deploy gates, or (b) a synthetic fork test PR verifies steps 1-3 and is closed unmerged while a real maintainer bundle verifies step 4 (no fake data ever merges into live Explorer).
context: Step 6 of the owner-approved Option 1 corpus consolidation plan (2026-11-24). End-to-end verification of Step 2 on a real fork PR into develop.
description:
## Problem
Unit tests cannot prove the full GitHub Actions interaction of `pull_request_target`, fork permissions, `develop` ruleset required checks, automatic `no-auto-merge` holding, and downstream `site-inputs.yml` -> `benchbox-site` deployment.

## Change
Execute an end-to-end verification of the Step 2 (`corpus-intake-on-develop-20261124`) fork submission flow into `develop`:
1. Open a test bundle submission PR from a fork into `develop` touching only `results-data/bundles/**` and `results-data/corpus-inventory.json`.
2. Confirm `validate-submission.yml` runs from trusted `develop` base code and posts its summary comment.
3. Confirm heavy code-test lanes are skipped while `develop`'s required ruleset checks complete cleanly.
4. Confirm auto-merge is mechanically blocked (`no-auto-merge` applied, `hold` blocks auto-merge, `make pr-arm` refuses).
5. Verify a negative fork check (or rely on Step 2's workflow test) that mixing a code edit with a bundle is rejected.
6. Confirm end-to-end publication into the next `site-inputs` bundle and passing `benchbox-site` deploy gates using an owner-approved real bundle (close any synthetic fork test PR unmerged).

## Decision gates
- NEVER merge a synthetic or dummy result bundle into `develop` or live Explorer. Only an owner-approved real benchmark bundle may be merged for step 6; close any synthetic fork test PR unmerged.
- Opening a fork PR from a separate GitHub account or owner fork may require owner action — stop and coordinate with the owner rather than spoofing or bypassing fork boundaries.
- Lifting a `no-auto-merge` hold on a PR requires explicit owner authorization naming that PR (`[MERGE-AUTHORITY-001]`).

## Verification rubric
- Pass: recorded PR URL(s), workflow run ID(s), and check snapshots showing (1) validator comment posted on fork PR, (2) heavy code lanes skipped, (3) `no-auto-merge` / `hold` blocking auto-merge, and (4) merged real bundle present in `site-inputs` artifact with passing `benchbox-site` deploy gates.
- Fail: verification uses only same-repo branches (never testing fork context), merges fake data into `results-data/`, or leaves a test PR open.

## Guardrails
No live cloud runs or credentials. Never bypass `hold`, `no-auto-merge`, or branch rulesets (`[MERGE-AUTHORITY-001]`). Record live run IDs and PR URLs directly in the closing note (`[EVIDENCE-FRESHNESS-001]`). Clean up any temporary fork branches and linked worktrees after verification.
